summary: A survey of the German generals, conservative politicians, judges, police, journalists, industrialists and Communists who, without being Nazis themselves, smoothed Hitler's path to power in Weimar Germany between 1918 and 1933.

evidence.note: story opens with the mid-1800s births and early careers of Hindenburg and Ludendorff
WWI segment: Tannenberg and the Hindenburg-Ludendorff silent dictatorship
1919 hearing where Hindenburg launches the stab-in-the-back myth
Beer Hall Putsch narrated, with Ludendorff marching beside Hitler
lenient police and judges: Neithardt's handling of the 1924 trial, Munich police protection
German and American press coverage that amplified or trivialised Hitler
parliamentary manoeuvring from Stresemann through Bruning, Papen and Schleicher
narrative ends with Hitler's appointment, the Enabling Act and Reichstag Fire Decree
detailed account of Hitler's attempted suicide after the putsch; Litten's later suicide

notes: Survey episode with no single bastard, so the primary subject is a group of enablers; Hindenburg, Ludendorff, Schleicher and Papen get the longest segments. Covered span starts at Hindenburg's 1847 birth because the opening spends several minutes on both generals' early lives; ends 1934 with the Night of the Long Knives deaths. The closing talk about modern US politics and police is comparison, so it is not counted.
